newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to set price limits on basic foods.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to set price limits on basic foods.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Thursday to impose maximum price limits on basic foods in a bid to curb soaring inflation boosted by a weakening lev and economic instablity.
"The government is introducing maximum acceptable prices for flour, cooking oil, milk and cheese," Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov told reporters after the cabinet's weekly meeting.
The highest acceptable price levels will be set after discussions with the respective producers' unions by September 12, he added. Prices on these foods could be adjusted monthly.
Consumer price inflation has soared to cumulative 82 percent for the first seven months after jumping 23.3 percent in July.
The government has pledged to curb monthly inflation to 2.5 percent by year-end.
But inflation in Bulgaria is closely linked to the lev/dollar exchange rate and inflation rate rises in direct proportion to the dollar rise against the local currency.
The lev lost 230 percent of its value against the dollar since the beginning of the year. It traded around 235 levs to the dollar on Thursday.

Thursday's decision to re-impose price controls is the first since February 1990, when the first post-communist interim government of Dimitar Popov lifted most price controls to offset a grave shortages.
